result.answer:
Verdict: REFUTED

Cell definitions and counts. The scoring specification says rows are true labels and columns are predictions [S:2e82301c3409#2] (source_1, p.1). It reports TP = 29, FP = 9, FN = 13, and TN = 59, with each test observation in exactly one cell [S:9b61eda5a361#2] (source_2, p.1).

Formulas. Positive-class F1 = 2TP/(2TP+FP+FN); negative-class F1 = 2TN/(2TN+FP+FN); macro-F1 = the arithmetic mean of the two class F1 scores [S:2e82301c3409#2]. The manuscript instead says it calculated 'macro-F1' as (TP+TN)/(TP+FP+FN+TN) and that no class averaging was performed [S:cd3c3f45fe5f#2] (source_3, p.1).

Recomputation:
- Positive F1 = 2(29)/(2(29)+9+13) = 58/80 = 29/40 = 0.725, using the counts [S:9b61eda5a361#2] and formula [S:2e82301c3409#2].
- Negative F1 = 2(59)/(2(59)+9+13) = 118/140 = 59/70 = 0.842857, using the counts [S:9b61eda5a361#2] and formula [S:2e82301c3409#2].
- Macro-F1 = (0.725 + 0.842857)/2 = 439/560 = 0.783929, using the class F1 definition [S:2e82301c3409#2].
- Accuracy = (29+59)/(29+9+13+59) = 88/110 = 4/5 = 0.8, using the manuscript's formula [S:cd3c3f45fe5f#2] and counts [S:9b61eda5a361#2].

The manuscript's label is not correct: its formula performs no class averaging [S:cd3c3f45fe5f#2], while macro-F1 is defined as the mean of the two class F1 scores [S:2e82301c3409#2]; the reported formula gives accuracy 0.8, not the macro-F1 value 0.783929.
